title: Mitigate microburst-induced scheduler crossover causing intermittent high-latency for multi-chunk requests
creator: Maya Patel
description: Summary: An enterprise customer (FalconPay) reported intermittent 2–8x latency spikes for large multi-chunk prompts (their reconciliation job uses 8–12k token sequences split into segments). This ticket tracks the production bugfix for an edge-case in our scheduler where in-flight segmented requests are rebalanced across hosts during short maintenance windows or transient capacity shifts, triggering KV cache eviction and a downstream admission amplification that dramatically increases tail latency for the affected sequences.
problem_statement: When a host signals ephemeral maintenance or is drained for scaling, the scheduler sometimes migrates an already-accepted segmented sequence to another host mid-flight. The migration path does not preserve sequence affinity or a short grace lease for KV cache entries; as a result the receiving host treats segments as new admissions, causing them to enter larger admission windows, lose cached KV state, and then be batched with long-running requests. The observable effect is a small subset of multi-chunk requests experiencing long tail latency spikes and repeat requeues under mixed-mode (hosted + dedicated + private) deployments.
root_cause_summary: Race between host drain path and admission lease expiry: the drain handshake preemptively marks inflight sequence tokens as transferable before KV cache checkpoint completes; receiving hosts apply normal admission scoring (which prefers throughput batches) and the sequence loses short-term affinity. Also, the admission re-enqueue logic lacks a bias to preserve sequences that already consumed large prefix state.
proposed_fix: 1) Introduce a short sequence-affinity lock (default 10s) during host drain to avoid mid-flight reassignment for segmented sequences; 2) Normalize admission lease times so that sequences with >1k prefix tokens get a longer grace lease; 3) Add a requeue scoring penalty to discourage immediate placement into throughput-dominant batches for reattached sequences; 4) Conservative KV-cache grace: delay eviction of recently-transferred sequence keys for 15s to allow checkpoints to complete; 5) Feature-flag the changes behind 'sequence-affinity-guard' and add a rollout plan.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for lock acquisition and release paths.
- Integration test: simulate host drain during active segmented sequence; assert sequence is not migrated until KV checkpoint/lock released.
- Stress test: synthetic mixed-length workload with microbursts (replicate customer traffic pattern); measure 99th and 99.9th percentile latency for multi-chunk sequences.
- Chaos test in staging: trigger node drain and abrupt host reboots while running fidelity workload.
- Private deployment smoke: run upgrade window simulation against a private cluster image to verify no state corruption.
rollout_plan: Canary -> staged ramp: 1% (internal) for 6h, 5% (non-critical customers) 12h, 25% 24h, 100% after metrics stable. Use feature flag 'sequence-affinity-guard' with ability to turn off instantly. If 99th percentile for multi-chunk sequences increases by >15% or error rate spikes, rollback immediately.
acceptance_criteria: Reproduction steps reliably fail before fix and succeed after in integration staging.
99th and 99.9th percentile latency for segmented requests in canary group decreases >= 40% compared to pre-fix under synthetic microburst tests.
No regression (>5%) on tail latency for short single-segment requests across hosted/dedicated/private mixing.
Monitoring dashboard surfaces a new 'sequence-affinity' metric and an alert for >3% reattach events per minute.
Customer FalconPay confirmation: no repeated escalations within 72h of full rollout and SLA targets met for their job windows.
comments: 2026-02-10: Customer FalconPay opened escalation — they saw intermittent 6–8s spikes on what should be 300–900ms jobs. They supplied a captured request trace and segment boundaries (CONF-1492 attached).

2026-02-11: Investigation: replicated microburst in staging by replaying FalconPay trace; confirmed migration occurs when ephemeral host-drain overlaps with KV flush window. Recorded trace in tracing: https://console.redwood.ai/traces/trace-FAKE-20260211

2026-02-11: RCA reviewed with infra and runtime leads (notes in Confluence, link below). Consensus: preserve affinity for active segmented sequences during drain and extend grace lease for large prefixes.
2026-02-12: Spike branch implemented with sequence-affinity lock and admission-lease normalization. Basic unit tests added. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12345

2026-02-12: Code review: feedback from @AnyaWu — tighten lock scope to avoid affecting short-lived single-chunk flows. @DiegoR suggested adding metric tags for 'reattach_reason' to improve post-rollout observability.
2026-02-13: Integration tests passed in staging. Stress test run shows 62% reduction in 99.9th latency for segmented sequences under synthetic microbursts. Preparing canary release.
2026-02-13: Customer update sent — initial patch scheduled to canary; asked FalconPay to hold non-critical jobs during canary window. Slack thread: #cust-falconpay-escalation
Postmortem action items drafted: add chaos tests for private upgrade windows, add telemetry for admission-requeue counts per tenant, update runbook for oncall to identify mid-flight migrations.
